argument_summary: The clean-compliance claim should be narrowed. The admissible record supports certification only in a constrained form: aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, but the current subgroup regression in loan modification support remains material and the present record does not show approved mitigation, risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language. Under the stated policy, prior approval and informal monitoring are context only. The defensible position is documentation-based certification with an explicit caveat that current release documentation must reflect the current evaluation result and disclose the subgroup limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis of this argument. The basis is that the audit concern can be handled as a bounded documentation-and-governance gap rather than as a broader challenge to aggregate readiness or the underlying certify_model decision.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit stale prior approval or informal monitoring to substitute for current-release documentation or approved mitigation. It does permit certification if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed, or if there is approved mitigation/risk acceptance. On the present admissible record, that supports caveated treatment rather than clean compliance.
concessions: The current record does not establish that the required disclosure is already present in the release documentation.
The current record does not contain approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for the loan modification weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration and current evaluation batch, so it cannot independently satisfy the current-release requirement.
